title: Identity normalization for ordinary open exchange
statement: Let (A,I) be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let j:U → T be an open immersion of schemes and sq an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square] whose horizontal maps are identities and whose two vertical maps are j. Write J for the exact derived extension by zero and e for the transported ordinary open exchange [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. For every K in d.derived U, e_K followed by J applied to the ordinary pullback identity [lem-weil-pbc-completed-ordinary-comparisons] on U equals the ordinary pullback identity on T evaluated at J(K). No compactification, finite-origin hypothesis, completeness, ideal-generating tuple, quasi-compactness or cohomological bound is required.

source.place: lemma-shriek-base-change: canonical conjugate of the sectionwise localization comparison; identity specialization. Derived transport as in cohomology.tex, section-derived-pullback.

proof.text: Use the underived identity for completed-ring module exchange. Compose each ordinary presentation transport with the datum pullback identity. The exact-derived counit normalization of cbcDatumOrdinaryTransport and the factorization formulas for mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryIdIso identify this composite on Q(P) with the ordinary resolving counit followed by Q of the termwise module identity. The functor equality cbcDatumModulePull_eq supplies exactly the equality transports in that normalization.

Form the candidate inverse derived exchange J(e_U) followed by e_T inverse at J. Naturality of e_T inverse moves it past the extension factorization. Postcompose with Q of the termwise ambient module identity, an isomorphism. The two counit-normalized identity formulas and the underived module square turn both sides into J of the ordinary resolving counit followed by its termwise identity; naturality of J.mapDerivedCategoryFactors completes the equation. Thus the candidate satisfies cbcDerivedInverseExchange_exists on every complex, in particular its required K-flat complexes. Its uniqueness identifies the actual inverse exchange with this candidate.

Precompose the required old-presentation exchange equation with the actual inverse exchange. The inverse law cancels that exchange, and the candidate formula cancels e_T inverse with e_T. Expand cbcDatumOrdinaryExchange and precompose with the ambient ordinary transport. Its hom/inv cancel. Functoriality expands J(e_U), giving the claimed identity with the original datum pullback identities.

lean.statement:
theorem cbcDatumOrdinaryExchange_identity
    {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    {U T : Scheme.{t}} (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (sq : OpenImmersionSquare (𝟙 U) j j (𝟙 T)) (K : d.derived U) :
    (cbcDatumOrdinaryExchange d sq).app K ≫
        (cbcDerivedOpenShriek d j inferInstance).map ((d.pullId U).hom.app K) =
      (d.pullId T).hom.app ((cbcDerivedOpenShriek d j inferInstance).obj K)
